name: Ajaymon
title: AI Product Designer
headline: I design fintech products that make complex financial workflows easier to use.
intro: Ajaymon, Junior Product Designer at Karbon Business. Fintech workflows, banking operations and design systems.
about: I'm Ajaymon, a product designer based in Bangalore. I design intuitive, accessible experiences across web and mobile, with a focus on making complex workflows feel simple. At Karbon Business, I work on fintech products, from customer dashboards to internal bank operations tools.

My process connects user research, wireframes, prototypes and high-fidelity interfaces with design systems and developer handoff. I collaborate with product, engineering and business teams, test ideas with users, and follow through with design QA. My background in data engineering brings an analytical lens to design, while AI opens new ways to explore, prototype and solve problems.

projects.title: Karbon Invoice Flow
projects.summary: Bringing invoice creation, review and payment reminders into one guided workflow
sections: Overview
Karbon Forex helps businesses and freelancers send and receive international payments. I worked on redesigning the platform to make complex remittance tasks easier to understand and complete.
The challenge

Users needed clearer navigation, better visibility into transactions and workflows that supported different business needs. Receivables, invoices, onboarding and outward payments all needed a more coherent experience.
Research and collaboration
I gathered feedback with customer-facing business and account management teams, worked with product managers and engineers, and refined designs through usability testing and internal feedback.
The approach

I designed simpler dashboards, clearer payment flows, customizable inward and outward workflows, and responsive interfaces. Wireframes and interactive prototypes helped validate the structure before high-fidelity design and developer handoff.
Systems and delivery
Reusable components, consistent visual hierarchy and design QA connected the interface design to implementation. The work included customer-facing screens and internal bank operations tools.
What I learned

Complex financial products benefit from clear input grouping, progressive disclosure and purposeful feedback. Staying close to users and collaborating early with engineering helps turn complicated requirements into usable experiences.
projects.problem: Users created invoices in other tools, uploaded PDFs to Karbon and shared payment details separately.
projects.contribution: Designed a guided invoice flow with payment-intent selection, a split-screen preview and separate compliance details.
projects.output: A proposed invoicing experience combining creation, review and reminder scheduling.
projects.collaborators: Product managers, engineers, business and account management teams
decisions: Start with payment intent
Separate one-time invoices, recurring invoices and payment links to support different invoicing needs.
Make the document visible
A split-screen preview gives the user a way to review the invoice alongside the form.
Separate amounts from compliance details
Grouping purpose-code information in a dedicated step reduces the number of different decisions on one screen.

projects.title: SWIFT Code Finder
projects.summary: A focused search and validation experience for international bank transfers
sections: Overview
A tool that helps people find or verify a bank's SWIFT/BIC code before making an international transfer.
The challenge
Finding the correct code often means searching multiple websites and cross-checking unfamiliar bank details. The experience needed to feel fast, clear and trustworthy.
Research
Research explored how people find SWIFT codes, what frustrates them and how well they understand the parts of a code. Trust, speed and help with validation shaped the design priorities.
The approach

I designed a country-to-bank-to-branch search flow, a code validation path, clear result states and a one-tap copy action. Short explanations help users understand codes without overwhelming the primary task.
Outcome
A mobile-friendly design that brings search, validation and education into a focused experience, with an emphasis on error prevention and clear feedback.
projects.problem: Finding a SWIFT code meant searching different sites and cross-checking unfamiliar bank details.
projects.contribution: Designed a country-to-bank-to-branch search, a validation path and clear result states.
projects.output: A mobile-friendly search and validation design with explanations and a one-tap copy action.
decisions: Guide the search in steps
Country, bank and branch provide a clear sequence for finding a code.
Give known codes a separate path
Validation supports people who already have a code and need to check it.
Explain without interrupting
Short explanations sit alongside results so the main task remains finding and using the code.

projects.title: Karbon Design System
projects.summary: Reusable components and shared foundations for a consistent fintech experience
sections: Overview
A shared design foundation for Karbon, connecting reusable UI components, typography, spacing, colors and iconography across product experiences.
The challenge
Inconsistent patterns and repeated component work made it harder for design and development teams to keep interfaces coherent as the product grew.
The process
I audited existing UI, defined principles around consistency and reuse, and worked with developers on components and documentation. Feedback from both teams guided iteration.
Tools and systems

The work connected Figma components with development patterns using Tailwind CSS, shadcn and Lucide icons. Exploration with v0 supported rapid component experiments while retaining a common visual language.
Outcome
A reusable component library and shared guidelines that support more consistent interfaces and a clearer handoff between design and engineering.
projects.problem: Inconsistent patterns and repeated component work made it harder to keep growing products coherent.
projects.contribution: Audited the UI and worked with developers on reusable components and documentation.
projects.output: A shared component library and guidelines spanning typography, spacing, colors and interface patterns.
decisions: Start with the existing interface
A UI audit grounds the shared foundations in patterns the product already needs.
Connect design to development
Figma components align with Tailwind CSS, shadcn and Lucide-based development patterns.
Make reuse understandable
Documentation and shared guidelines accompany the components to support a clearer handoff.

headline: One product language.
Many moving parts.
story.problem_heading: As the product grew, the patterns drifted.
story.context: Repeated component work and inconsistent interface patterns made it harder for design and development to keep the product coherent. The design system work focused on giving those repeated decisions a shared foundation.

fourth_decision: Keep feedback part of the system
Feedback from design and development informs the library. A component needs to work across the product’s use cases, not only look consistent in one screen.

projects.title: Karbon Business
projects.summary: A clearer, responsive web experience for a complex financial product
projects.tags: Web design · Responsive UX · Visual design
sections: Overview
A redesign of the Karbon Business web experience, focused on communicating the product clearly and helping visitors find the information they need.
The challenge
The existing experience needed stronger navigation, a more deliberate content hierarchy and a responsive interface that communicated the product's capabilities.
The approach
Research and discovery informed streamlined navigation, clearer typography and a mobile-first structure. Consistent visual patterns brought product information into a more cohesive story.
Design priorities
I focused on user-centric navigation, readable product information, responsive layouts and clear visual hierarchy, working across content and interface decisions.
Outcome
A more coherent web experience that makes a complex financial product easier to explore and understand.
projects.problem: Visitors needed clearer navigation and a better hierarchy to understand a complex financial product.
projects.contribution: Refined navigation, typography and responsive layouts across the Karbon Business web experience.
projects.output: A responsive interface with a more coherent structure for product information.
decisions: Structure information around navigation
Streamlined navigation and clearer hierarchy help visitors find relevant product information.
Design for smaller screens
A mobile-first structure informs responsive layouts rather than treating them as an afterthought.
Use a consistent visual language
Shared typography and interface patterns bring separate product sections into a coherent experience.
